section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes a single study of college women examining interpersonal (attachment, caregiver eating messages) and intrapersonal (maladaptive/adaptive perfectionism) predictors of body appreciation and its links to depressive symptoms and intuitive eating. The model accounted for sizable variance in body appreciation and intuitive eating, with body appreciation mediating several relationships; depressive symptoms were related in bivariate analyses but did not account for unique variance once other predictors were included.
section_summary.evidence_source: "In this study, we explored a model including potential interpersonal (i.e., adult attachment, caregiver eating messages) and intrapersonal (i.e., maladaptive and adaptive perfectionism) barriers and facilitators to body appreciation as well as body appreciation's ties to two indices of well-being (i.e., depressive symptoms and intuitive eating)." Also: "Overall, this model provided a good foundation from which to understand college women's body appreciation and its connection to intuitive eating. The model constructs contributed 40.5% of the variance in body appreciation."
